drills.solution: $(f^{-1})'(b) = \dfrac{1}{f'(a)}$ where $f(a) = b$. Here $f({p}) = {bv}$, and $f'(x) = 3x^2 {a:signed}$, so $f'({p}) = {d}$. Therefore $(f^{-1})'({bv}) =$ **{r:frac}**. (Evaluate $f'$ at ${p}$, not at ${bv}$.)

drills.title: Related rates for a sphere
drills.prompt: Air is pumped into a spherical balloon at {dv} cm³/s. How fast is the radius increasing when the radius is {r} cm? (cm/s, 4 decimals)
drills.solution: $V = \tfrac43\pi r^3$, so $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt}$. Substitute: ${dv} = 4\pi({r})^2\dfrac{dr}{dt} = {k}\pi\,\dfrac{dr}{dt}$. So $\dfrac{dr}{dt} = \dfrac{{dv}}{{k}\pi} \approx$ **{rate:num4}** cm/s.

drills.title: Sliding ladder
drills.prompt: A {L}-ft ladder leans against a wall. Its foot slides away from the wall at {v} ft/s. How fast is the top sliding down when the foot is {x} ft from the wall? (exact fraction, ft/s)
drills.solution: $x^2 + y^2 = {L}^2$. Differentiate in $t$: $2x\dfrac{dx}{dt} + 2y\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 0$. When $x = {x}$, $y = \sqrt{{L}^2 - {x}^2} = {y}$. So ${x}({v}) + {y}\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 0$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -\dfrac{{xv}}{{y}}$. The top slides down at **{rate:frac}** ft/s.

drills.title: Estimate a square root by linearization
drills.prompt: Use the linearization of $f(x) = \sqrt x$ at $a = {a}$ to estimate $\sqrt{{xx}}$. (4 decimals)
drills.solution: $f({a}) = {n}$ and $f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt x}$, so $f'({a}) = \dfrac{1}{{n2}}$. Then $L(x) = {n} + \dfrac{1}{{n2}}(x - {a})$ and $L({xx}) = {n} + \dfrac{1}{{n2}}({d}) \approx$ **{L:num4}**. (Actual: {tru:num4}; $\sqrt x$ is concave down, so the estimate is a little high.)

drills.title: Two steps of Newton's method
drills.prompt: Apply Newton's method to $f(x) = x^3 {a:signedcoef}x - {b}$ starting from $x_0 = {x0}$. Find $x_1$ and $x_2$ (4 decimals).
drills.solution:
$f'(x) = 3x^2 {a:signed}$ and $x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}$.
- $x_1 = {x0} - \dfrac{{f0}}{{d0}} \approx$ **{x1:num4}**
- $x_2 = x_1 - \dfrac{f(x_1)}{f'(x_1)} \approx {x1:num4} - \dfrac{{f1:num4}}{{d1:num4}} \approx$ **{x2:num4}**

(The root is about {root:num4}.)

drills.title: L'Hôpital's rule twice
drills.prompt: Find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\frac{1 - \cos({a}x)}{{b}^2x^2}$ as an exact fraction.
drills.solution: The form is $0/0$. L'Hôpital: $\dfrac{{a}\sin({a}x)}{2\cdot{b}^2x}$, still $0/0$. Again: $\dfrac{{a2}\cos({a}x)}{{b2}} \to \dfrac{{a2}}{{b2}} =$ **{L:frac}**.

drills.title: A 1^∞ limit
drills.prompt: Find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}\left(1 {a:signed}/x\right)^{{b:coef}x}$. (Exact, like e^3, or to 5 significant figures.)
drills.solution: This is $1^\infty$. Let $y$ be the expression; $\ln y = {b:coef}x\ln\left(1 {a:signed}/x\right) = \dfrac{{b:coef}\ln(1 {a:signed}/x)}{1/x}$, a $0/0$ form. L'Hôpital: $\dfrac{{b:coef}\frac{1}{1 {a:signed}/x}\cdot\left({na:coef}\frac{1}{x^2}\right)}{-\frac{1}{x^2}} = \dfrac{{p}}{1 {a:signed}/x} \to {p}$. So $y \to$ **$e^{{p}}$** $\approx$ {L:sig5}.

drills.title: Absolute extrema on a closed interval

calc.mx: max(f(r1 - left), f(r1), f(r1 + gap), f(r1 + gap + right))
calc.mn: min(f(r1 - left), f(r1), f(r1 + gap), f(r1 + gap + right))

drills.prompt: Find the absolute maximum and minimum values of $f(x) = x^3 {b:signedcoef}x^2 {c:signedcoef}x {d:signed}$ on $[{lo}, {hi}]$.
drills.solution:
$f'(x) = 3x^2 {b2:signedcoef}x {c:signed} = 3(x {nr1:signed})(x {nr2:signed})$, so the critical numbers are ${r1}$ and ${r2}$, both in the interval. Evaluate at critical numbers and endpoints:

| $x$ | ${lo}$ | ${r1}$ | ${r2}$ | ${hi}$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $f(x)$ | {flo} | {f1} | {f2} | {fhi} |

Absolute max **{mx}**, absolute min **{mn}**.

drills.title: Find c in the Mean Value Theorem
drills.prompt: Find the number $c$ in $({p}, {q})$ that satisfies the Mean Value Theorem for $f(x) = x^3$ on $[{p}, {q}]$. (4 decimals)
drills.solution: Average rate: $\dfrac{{fq} - {fp}}{{q} - {p}} = {avg}$. Set $f'(c) = 3c^2 = {avg}$: $c = \sqrt{{avg}/3} \approx$ **{c:num4}**, which lies in $({p}, {q})$. (The negative root is outside the interval.)

drills.title: Locate the local max and min
drills.prompt: For $f(x) = 2x^3 {b:signedcoef}x^2 {c:signedcoef}x$, find where $f$ has its local maximum and local minimum.
drills.solution: $f'(x) = 6x^2 {b2:signedcoef}x {c:signed} = 6(x {nr1:signed})(x {nr2:signed})$. Sign chart: $f' > 0$ for $x < {r1}$, $f' < 0$ between ${r1}$ and ${r2}$, $f' > 0$ for $x > {r2}$. So $f$ has a local max at $x =$ **{r1}** ($+$ to $-$) and a local min at $x =$ **{r2}** ($-$ to $+$).

drills.title: Local maximum of a power times an exponential
drills.prompt: Find the location and value of the local maximum of $f(x) = x^{n}e^{-x/{k}}$ for $x > 0$. (Value to 4 significant figures.)
drills.solution: Product and chain rules: $f'(x) = {n}x^{{n1}}e^{-x/{k}} - \tfrac{1}{{k}}x^{n}e^{-x/{k}} = x^{{n1}}e^{-x/{k}}\left({n} - \tfrac{x}{{k}}\right)$. For $x > 0$ the first two factors are positive, so the sign of $f'$ is the sign of ${n} - x/{k}$: positive before $x = {xm}$, negative after. Local max at $x =$ **{xm}**, value $f({xm}) = {xm}^{n}e^{-{n}} \approx$ **{ym:sig4}**.

drills.title: Inflection point of a cubic
drills.prompt: Find the inflection point of $f(x) = x^3 {b:signedcoef}x^2 {b1:signedcoef}x {d:signed}$.
drills.solution: $f'(x) = 3x^2 {b2:signedcoef}x {b1:signed}$ and $f''(x) = 6x {b2:signed}$, which is zero at $x = {h}$ and changes sign there (negative before, positive after). The inflection point is $({h}, f({h}))$ = **({h}, {yi})**.

drills.title: Second derivative test
drills.prompt: Use the second derivative test to find the local maximum and local minimum values of $f(x) = x^3 - {a2}x {c:signed}$.

drills.title: Open box of largest volume
drills.prompt: Squares of side $x$ are cut from the corners of a {W}-in by {L}-in sheet, and the sides are folded up to make an open box. Find the $x$ that maximizes the volume, and the maximum volume. (3 decimals for $x$; volume to the nearest 0.1 in³)
drills.solution: $V(x) = x({W} - 2x)({L} - 2x) = 4x^3 - {s4}x^2 + {wl}x$ on $0 \le x \le {hw}$. $V'(x) = 12x^2 - {s8}x + {wl} = 0$. The quadratic formula gives two roots; the smaller, $x \approx$ **{x:dp3}**, is in the domain (the larger exceeds {hw}). Endpoints give $V = 0$, so the max is $V \approx$ **{Vm:num1}** in³.

drills.title: Least fence for a riverside pen
drills.prompt: A rectangular pen along a straight river must enclose {A:int} m². No fence is needed along the river. What dimensions minimize the fencing, and how much fence is used?
drills.solution: With $x$ perpendicular and $y$ parallel: $xy = {A:dp0}$, so $y = {A:dp0}/x$, and the fence is $F(x) = 2x + \dfrac{{A:dp0}}{x}$ for $x > 0$. $F'(x) = 2 - \dfrac{{A:dp0}}{x^2} = 0$ gives $x^2 = {A:dp0}/2$, $x =$ **{px}**. $F''(x) = \dfrac{2\cdot{A:dp0}}{x^3} > 0$, so it's the minimum. Then $y =$ **{py}** and $F =$ **{F}** m.

drills.title: Antiderivative of powers
drills.prompt: Find $\displaystyle\int\left({a}x^{n} {b:signedcoef}x + \frac{{c}}{x^2}\right)dx$. (Leave off $+C$.)
drills.solution:
Rewrite $\dfrac{{c}}{x^2} = {c:coef}x^{-2}$ and raise each exponent by one, dividing by the new exponent:
$${a}\cdot\frac{x^{{n1}}}{{n1}} {b:signed}\cdot\frac{x^2}{2} + {c}\cdot\frac{x^{-1}}{-1} + C.$$
So **$F(x) = {an:texfrac}x^{{n1}} {hb:signedcoef}x^2 - \dfrac{{c}}{x} + C$**.

drills.title: Initial value problem
drills.prompt: Solve the initial value problem $f'(x) = {a3}x^2 {b2:signedcoef}x {c:signed}$, $f({p}) = {q}$.
drills.solution: Antidifferentiate: $f(x) = {a:coef}x^3 {b:signedcoef}x^2 {c:signedcoef}x + C$. Apply $f({p}) = {q}$: ${base} + C = {q}$, so $C = {K}$. Therefore **$f(x) = {a:coef}x^3 {b:signedcoef}x^2 {c:signedcoef}x {K:signed}$**.

drills.title: Riemann sum with four rectangles
drills.prompt: Approximate $\displaystyle\int_{{lo}}^{{hi}}\left({a:coef}x^2 + {c}\right)dx$ with a {w} Riemann sum using $n = 4$ subintervals. (Round to 4 decimals if needed.)
drills.solution: $\Delta x = \dfrac{{hi} - {lo}}{4} = {dx}$. The {w} sample points are ${p1}, {p2}, {p3}, {p4}$, with heights {h1:num4}, {h2:num4}, {h3:num4}, {h4:num4}. Sum: ${dx}\times({h1:num4} + {h2:num4} + {h3:num4} + {h4:num4}) =$ **{S:num4}**. (The exact integral is {ex:num4}.)

drills.title: Evaluate a sum with sigma formulas
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{{n}}\left({a:coef}i^2 {b:signed}\right)$.
drills.solution:
Split and use $\sum_{i=1}^n i^2 = \dfrac{n(n + 1)(2n + 1)}{6}$ and $\sum_{i=1}^n 1 = n$:
$${a}\cdot\frac{{n}\cdot({n} + 1)(2\cdot{n} + 1)}{6} {b:signed}\cdot{n} = {a}\cdot{s2:dp0} {bn:signed} = \mathbf{{S:dp0}}.$$

drills.title: Definite integral by geometry
drills.prompt: Use geometry to evaluate $\displaystyle\int_{-{r}}^{{r}}\left({k} + \sqrt{{r2} - x^2}\right)dx$. (Exact, like 9pi/2 + 12, or 4 decimals.)
drills.solution: Split the integral. $\int_{-{r}}^{{r}}{k}\,dx$ is a rectangle ${d} \times {k}$ with area ${rect}$. $\int_{-{r}}^{{r}}\sqrt{{r2} - x^2}\,dx$ is the area of the upper half of a circle of radius ${r}$: $\tfrac12\pi({r})^2$. Total: ${rect} + \dfrac{{r2}\pi}{2} \approx$ **{A:num4}**.

drills.title: Evaluate a definite integral
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_{{p}}^{{q}}\left({a:coef}x^2 {b:signedcoef}x {c:signed}\right)dx$ as an exact fraction.
drills.solution: An antiderivative is $F(x) = {a:coef}\dfrac{x^3}{3} {b:signedcoef}\dfrac{x^2}{2} {c:signedcoef}x$. By FTC 2, $F({q}) - F({p}) = {Fq:frac} - ({Fp:frac}) =$ **{I:frac}**.

drills.title: Derivative of an integral with a variable limit
drills.prompt: Find $\dfrac{d}{dx}\displaystyle\int_{{a}}^{x^{n}}\sqrt{t^2 + {k}}\,dt$.
drills.solution: FTC 1 with the chain rule: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\int_a^{u(x)}f(t)\,dt = f(u(x))\,u'(x)$. Here $u = x^{n}$, $u' = {n}x^{{n1}}$, and $f(u) = \sqrt{(x^{n})^2 + {k}}$. So the derivative is **${n}x^{{n1}}\sqrt{x^{{n2}} + {k}}$**.

drills.title: Substitution in an indefinite integral
drills.prompt: Find $\displaystyle\int {a}x\left(x^2 + {b}\right)^{n}\,dx$. (Leave off $+C$.)
drills.solution:
Let $u = x^2 + {b}$, so $du = 2x\,dx$ and $x\,dx = \tfrac12du$. Then
$$\int{a}x(x^2 + {b})^{n}dx = \frac{{a}}{2}\int u^{n}du = \frac{{a}}{2}\cdot\frac{u^{{n1}}}{{n1}} + C.$$
So **$F(x) = {co:texfrac}(x^2 + {b})^{{n1}} + C$**.

drills.title: Substitution in a definite integral
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^{{p}}\frac{2x}{x^2 + {k}}\,dx$. (Exact, like ln(5), or 4 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Let $u = x^2 + {k}$, $du = 2x\,dx$. Change the limits: $x = 0 \Rightarrow u = {k}$; $x = {p} \Rightarrow u = {up}$.
$$\int_{{k}}^{{up}}\frac{du}{u} = \ln {up} - \ln {k} = \ln\frac{{up}}{{k}} \approx \mathbf{{I:num4}}.$$

drills.title: When a particle turns around
drills.prompt: A particle moves with position $s(t) = t^3 {b:signedcoef}t^2 {c:signedcoef}t$ for $t \ge 0$. At what two times does it change direction? What is its acceleration at $t = {T}$?
drills.solution: $v(t) = 3t^2 {b2:signedcoef}t {c:signed} = 3(t - {r1})(t - {r2})$, which changes sign at $t =$ **{r1}** and $t =$ **{r2}**. $a(t) = v'(t) = 6t {b2:signed}$, so $a({T}) =$ **{aT}**. (At that moment $v({T}) = {vT}$.)

drills.title: Displacement and total distance
drills.prompt: A particle has velocity $v(t) = t - {c}$ m/s. Find its displacement and the total distance it travels on $0 \le t \le {b}$.
drills.solution: Displacement $= \int_0^{{b}}(t - {c})\,dt = \left[\tfrac{t^2}{2} - {c}t\right]_0^{{b}} =$ **{disp}** m. For distance, split at $t = {c}$ where $v$ changes sign: the triangle below the axis has area {back} and the one above has area {fwd}, so the distance is ${back} + {fwd} =$ **{dist}** m.

drills.title: Average value of a function
drills.prompt: Find the average value of $f(x) = {a:coef}x^2 {b:signed}$ on $[0, {c}]$ (exact fraction), and the $x$ in $[0, {c}]$ where $f$ equals its average (4 decimals).
drills.solution: $f_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{1}{{c}}\displaystyle\int_0^{{c}}({a:coef}x^2 {b:signed})\,dx = \dfrac{1}{{c}}\left[\dfrac{{a:coef}x^3}{3} {b:signedcoef}x\right]_0^{{c}} = \dfrac{1}{{c}}\cdot{I:texfrac} =$ **{fav:frac}**. Solve ${a:coef}x^2 {b:signed} = {fav:texfrac}$: $x^2 = \dfrac{{c}^2}{3}$, so $x = \dfrac{{c}}{\sqrt3} \approx$ **{xc:num4}**.

drills.title: Trapezoidal and left sums from uneven data
drills.prompt:
Water flows into a tank at rate $r(t)$ liters per minute. Measurements:

| $t$ (min) | 0 | {t1} | {t2} | {t3} |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $r(t)$ (L/min) | {r0} | {r1} | {r2} | {r3} |

Estimate $\displaystyle\int_0^{{t3}} r(t)\,dt$ with a trapezoidal sum and with a left Riemann sum, using the subintervals in the table.
drills.solution:
The widths are {w1}, {w2} and {w3} minutes; each piece uses its own width.

*Trapezoidal:* $\dfrac{{r0} + {r1}}{2}({w1}) + \dfrac{{r1} + {r2}}{2}({w2}) + \dfrac{{r2} + {r3}}{2}({w3}) = {p1} + {p2} + {p3} =$ **{T:num1}** liters.

*Left sum:* ${r0}({w1}) + {r1}({w2}) + {r2}({w3}) =$ **{Lsum}** liters.

drills.title: Complete the square, then arctan
drills.prompt: Write $x^2 {b:signedcoef}x + {c}$ as $(x + h)^2 + k^2$ with $k > 0$, then evaluate $\displaystyle\int_{{lo}}^{{hi}}\frac{dx}{x^2 {b:signedcoef}x + {c}}$. (Exact, like pi/8, or 4 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Half of ${b}$ is ${h}$, and $(x {h:signed})^2 = x^2 {b:signedcoef}x + {hh}$. So
$$x^2 {b:signedcoef}x + {c} = (x {h:signed})^2 + {k2},$$
which gives $h =$ **{h}** and $k =$ **{k}**.

Let $u = x {h:signed}$, so $du = dx$; the limits $x = {lo}$ and $x = {hi}$ become $u = {U1}$ and $u = {U2}$. Then
$$\int_{{U1}}^{{U2}}\frac{du}{u^2 + {k2}} = \frac{1}{{k}}\left[\arctan\frac{u}{{k}}\right]_{{U1}}^{{U2}} = \frac{1}{{k}}\left(\arctan({uhi}) - \arctan({ulo})\right) = \frac{\pi}{{den}} \approx \mathbf{{V:num4}}.$$

drills.title: Area between a parabola and a line
drills.prompt: Find the area of the region between $y = x^2$ and $y = {m:coef}x {k:signed}$. (Exact fraction.)
drills.solution:
Intersections: $x^2 = {m:coef}x {k:signed}$ gives $(x {nr1:signed})(x {nr2:signed}) = 0$, so $x = {r1}$ and $x = {r2}$. Between them the line is on top. 
$$A = \int_{{r1}}^{{r2}}\left({m:coef}x {k:signed} - x^2\right)dx = \frac{{gap}^3}{6} = \mathbf{{A:texfrac}}.$$
(For a line cutting a parabola $y = x^2$ at $x = p$ and $x = q$, the area is always $\frac{(q - p)^3}{6}$.)

drills.title: Area with horizontal slices
drills.prompt: Find the area of the region between the curve $x = {a:coef}y({k} - y)$ and the $y$-axis. (Exact fraction.)
drills.solution:
The curve meets the $y$-axis ($x = 0$) at $y = 0$ and $y = {k}$, and is to the right of it in between. Horizontal slices: right minus left is ${a:coef}y({k} - y) - 0$.
$$A = \int_0^{{k}}\left({ak:coef}y - {a:coef}y^2\right)dy = \frac{{ak}\cdot{k}^2}{2} - \frac{{a}\cdot{k}^3}{3} = \mathbf{{A:texfrac}}.$$

drills.title: Volume by disks
drills.prompt: The region under $y = {n}$ for $0 \le x \le {b}$ is rotated about the $x$-axis. Find the volume. (Exact, like 8pi/3, or 3 decimals.)
drills.solution: Disks of radius $R = {n}$: $V = \pi\displaystyle\int_0^{{b}}\left({n}\right)^2dx = \pi\int_0^{{b}}x^{{p1}}\,dx = \pi\cdot\frac{{b}^{{p}}}{{p}} \approx$ **{V:num4}** (that is, ${c:num4}\pi$).

drills.title: Volume by washers
drills.prompt: The region between $y = {m:coef}x$ and $y = x^2$ is rotated about the $x$-axis. Find the volume. (Exact or 3 decimals.)
drills.solution:
The curves meet at $x = 0$ and $x = {m}$; the line is farther from the axis. Washers with $R = {m:coef}x$, $r = x^2$:
$$V = \pi\int_0^{{m}}\left({m2:coef}x^2 - x^4\right)dx = \pi\left(\frac{{m2}\cdot{m}^3}{3} - \frac{{m}^5}{5}\right) = \frac{2\cdot{m5}\,\pi}{15} \approx \mathbf{{V:num4}}.$$

drills.title: Volume with known cross sections
drills.prompt: The base of a solid is the triangle with vertices $(0, 0)$, $({b}, 0)$ and $(0, {h})$. Cross sections perpendicular to the $x$-axis are {shape}. Find the volume. (4 significant figures.)
drills.solution: At position $x$ the base runs from $y = 0$ up to the hypotenuse $y = {h}\left(1 - \tfrac{x}{{b}}\right)$, so the side is $s = {h}\left(1 - \tfrac{x}{{b}}\right)$. Then $\int_0^{{b}}s^2\,dx = \dfrac{{h}^2\cdot{b}}{3} = {base:num4}$. The area of each cross section is $s^2$ times a constant (1 for squares, $\frac\pi8$ for semicircles, $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}$ for equilateral triangles), so $V \approx$ **{V:sig4}**.

drills.title: Volume by shells
drills.prompt: The region between $y = {a:coef}x - x^2$ and the $x$-axis is rotated about the line $x = -{k}$. Use shells to find the volume. (Exact or 3 decimals.)
drills.solution:
The region spans $0 \le x \le {a}$. A vertical strip at $x$ has height ${a:coef}x - x^2$ and distance $x + {k}$ from the axis $x = -{k}$.
$$V = 2\pi\int_0^{{a}}(x + {k})({a:coef}x - x^2)\,dx \approx \mathbf{{V:num4}}.$$
(Expanding: $2\pi\left[\frac{{a}^4}{12} + {k}\cdot\frac{{a}^3}{6}\right]$.)

drills.title: Arc length of a parabola (numerical)
drills.prompt: Set up and evaluate (with a calculator) the length of $y = {a:coef}x^2$ from $x = 0$ to $x = {b}$. (3 decimals)
drills.solution: $y' = {ad:coef}x$, so $L = \displaystyle\int_0^{{b}}\sqrt{1 + {a2:coef}x^2}\,dx \approx$ **{L:dp3}**. Check: the straight chord from $(0, 0)$ to the endpoint has length {chord:dp3}, and the curve is a bit longer.

drills.title: Surface area of revolution
drills.prompt: Find the area of the surface formed by rotating $y = \sqrt x$, $0 \le x \le {b}$, about the $x$-axis. (3 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$y' = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt x}$, so $y\sqrt{1 + (y')^2} = \sqrt x\sqrt{1 + \dfrac{1}{4x}} = \sqrt{x + \tfrac14}$.
$$S = 2\pi\int_0^{{b}}\sqrt{x + \tfrac14}\,dx = 2\pi\cdot\frac23\left[\left(x + \tfrac14\right)^{3/2}\right]_0^{{b}} = \frac{\pi}{6}\left({b4}^{3/2} - 1\right) \approx \mathbf{{S:dp3}}.$$

drills.title: Work stretching a spring
drills.prompt: A force of {F} N holds a spring stretched {d} cm beyond its natural length. How much work (in joules) does it take to stretch it from {s1} cm to {s2} cm beyond natural length? (4 significant figures.)
drills.solution:
Convert to meters. $k = \dfrac{{F}}{{d}/100} = {k:dp2}$ N/m. Then
$$W = \int_{{m1}}^{{m2}}{k:dp2}\,x\,dx = \frac{{k:dp2}}{2}\left({m2}^2 - {m1}^2\right) \approx \mathbf{{W:sig4}}\text{ J}.$$

drills.title: Work to pump out a tank
drills.prompt: A cylindrical tank with radius {r} m and height {H} m is full of water. How much work is needed to pump all the water to a point {o} m above the top of the tank? Use $\rho g = 9800$ N/m³. (3 significant figures, in J.)
drills.solution:
Put $y = 0$ at the bottom. A layer at height $y$ has volume $\pi({r})^2\,dy$, weight $9800\pi\cdot{r2}\,dy$, and is lifted to height ${top}$, a distance ${top} - y$.
$$W = \int_0^{{H}}9800\pi\cdot{r2}\,({top} - y)\,dy = 9800\pi\cdot{r2}\left({top}\cdot{H} - \frac{{H}^2}{2}\right) \approx \mathbf{{W:texsci}}\text{ J}.$$

drills.title: Centroid of the region under a power
drills.prompt: Find the centroid $(\bar x, \bar y)$ of the region under $y = x^{n}$ for $0 \le x \le {b}$. (Exact fractions.)
drills.solution: $A = \displaystyle\int_0^{{b}}x^{n}dx = {A:texfrac}$. Moments: $\displaystyle\int_0^{{b}}x\cdot x^{n}dx = {Mx:texfrac}$ and $\displaystyle\int_0^{{b}}\tfrac12x^{2\cdot{n}}dx = {My:texfrac}$. Divide by $A$: $\bar x =$ **{xb:frac}**, $\bar y =$ **{yb:frac}**.

drills.title: Integration by parts with a logarithm
drills.prompt: Find $\displaystyle\int {a:coef}{n}\ln x\,dx$ for $x > 0$. (Leave off $+C$; type ln for the natural log.)
drills.solution:
LIATE: $u = \ln x$, $dv = {n}\,dx$, so $du = \dfrac{dx}{x}$ and $v = \dfrac{x^{{n1}}}{{n1}}$.
$$\int {n}\ln x\,dx = \frac{x^{{n1}}}{{n1}}\ln x - \int\frac{x^{{n1}}}{{n1}}\cdot\frac1x\,dx = \frac{x^{{n1}}}{{n1}}\ln x - \frac{x^{{n1}}}{{sq}} + C.$$
Multiply by ${a}$: **$F(x) = {a:coef}\left(\dfrac{x^{{n1}}}{{n1}}\ln x - \dfrac{x^{{n1}}}{{sq}}\right) + C$**.

drills.title: Definite integral by parts
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^{{b}}x\,e^{-{k:coef}x}\,dx$. (4 decimals)
drills.solution:
$u = x$, $dv = e^{-{k:coef}x}dx$, so $du = dx$, $v = -\tfrac{1}{{k}}e^{-{k:coef}x}$.
$$\int_0^{{b}}xe^{-{k:coef}x}dx = \left[-\frac{x}{{k}}e^{-{k:coef}x}\right]_0^{{b}} + \frac{1}{{k}}\int_0^{{b}}e^{-{k:coef}x}dx = \left[-\frac{x}{{k}}e^{-{k:coef}x} - \frac{1}{{k2}}e^{-{k:coef}x}\right]_0^{{b}}.$$
$= \dfrac{1}{{k2}} - \left(\dfrac{{b}}{{k}} + \dfrac{1}{{k2}}\right)e^{-{kb}} \approx$ **{I:num4}**.

drills.title: Odd power of sine
drills.prompt: Find $\displaystyle\int\sin^3x\cos^{n}x\,dx$. (Leave off $+C$; type cos(x)^k for powers.)
drills.solution:
The sine power is odd: save one $\sin x$ and write $\sin^2x = 1 - \cos^2x$. With $u = \cos x$, $du = -\sin x\,dx$:
$$\int(1 - \cos^2x)\cos^{n}x\,\sin x\,dx = -\int(u^{n} - u^{{n2}})\,du = -\frac{u^{{n1}}}{{n1}} + \frac{u^{{n3}}}{{n3}} + C.$$
So **$F(x) = -\dfrac{\cos^{{n1}}x}{{n1}} + \dfrac{\cos^{{n3}}x}{{n3}} + C$**.

drills.title: Trigonometric substitution
drills.prompt: Find $\displaystyle\int\frac{dx}{(x^2 + {a2})^{3/2}}$. (Leave off $+C$.)
drills.solution:
Let $x = {a}\tan\theta$, $dx = {a}\sec^2\theta\,d\theta$, and $x^2 + {a2} = {a2}\sec^2\theta$, so $(x^2 + {a2})^{3/2} = {a}^3\sec^3\theta$.
$$\int\frac{{a}\sec^2\theta}{{a}^3\sec^3\theta}\,d\theta = \frac{1}{{a2}}\int\cos\theta\,d\theta = \frac{1}{{a2}}\sin\theta + C.$$
Triangle: $\tan\theta = \dfrac{x}{{a}}$, hypotenuse $\sqrt{x^2 + {a2}}$, so $\sin\theta = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^2 + {a2}}}$. **$F(x) = \dfrac{x}{{a2}\sqrt{x^2 + {a2}}} + C$**.

drills.title: Partial fractions with two linear factors
drills.prompt: Find $\displaystyle\int\frac{{p:coef}x {q:signed}}{x^2 {s:signedcoef}x {t:signed}}\,dx$. (Leave off $+C$. Type logs as ln(abs(...)) or ln(...).)
drills.solution: Factor: $x^2 {s:signedcoef}x {t:signed} = (x {nr1:signed})(x {nr2:signed})$. Set $\dfrac{{p:coef}x {q:signed}}{(x {nr1:signed})(x {nr2:signed})} = \dfrac{A}{x {nr1:signed}} + \dfrac{B}{x {nr2:signed}}$ and clear denominators: ${p:coef}x {q:signed} = A(x {nr2:signed}) + B(x {nr1:signed})$. Plug in $x = {r1}$ to get $A = {cA}$, and $x = {r2}$ to get $B = {cB}$. Integrate: **$F(x) = {cA:coef}\ln|x {nr1:signed}| {cB:signedcoef}\ln|x {nr2:signed}| + C$**.

drills.title: Trapezoidal rule
drills.prompt: Use the trapezoidal rule with $n = 4$ to approximate $\displaystyle\int_0^{{b}}\frac{1}{1 + x^2}\,dx$. (4 decimals)
drills.solution:
$\Delta x = {h4}$. Values: $f(0) = {y0:num4}$, $f({h4}) = {y1:num4}$, $f({hb}) = {y2:num4}$, $f({t3}) = {y3:num4}$, $f({b}) = {y4:num4}$.
$$T_4 = \frac{{h4}}{2}\left[{y0:num4} + 2({y1:num4}) + 2({y2:num4}) + 2({y3:num4}) + {y4:num4}\right] \approx \mathbf{{T:num4}}.$$
(Exact: $\arctan {b} \approx {ex:num4}$.)

drills.title: Simpson's rule
drills.prompt: Use Simpson's rule with $n = 4$ to approximate $\displaystyle\int_0^{{b}}\sqrt{1 + x^3}\,dx$. (4 decimals)
drills.solution:
$\Delta x = {h4}$. Values: {y0:num4}, {y1:num4}, {y2:num4}, {y3:num4}, {y4:num4}. Weights $1, 4, 2, 4, 1$:
$$S_4 = \frac{{h4}}{3}\left[{y0:num4} + 4({y1:num4}) + 2({y2:num4}) + 4({y3:num4}) + {y4:num4}\right] \approx \mathbf{{S:num4}}.$$
(A high-precision value is {ex:num4}.)

drills.title: Convergent improper integral
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_1^\infty\frac{{k}}{x^{p}}\,dx$ as an exact fraction.
drills.solution:
$$\int_1^\infty {k:coef}x^{-{p}}dx = \lim_{t\to\infty}\left[\frac{{k:coef}x^{-{p1}}}{-{p1}}\right]_1^t = \lim_{t\to\infty}\left(\frac{{k}}{{p1}} - \frac{{k}}{{p1}\,t^{{p1}}}\right) = \frac{{k}}{{p1}}.$$
It converges ($p = {p} > 1$) to **{I:frac}**.

drills.title: Improper integral with an infinite discontinuity
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^{{b}}\frac{{k}}{\sqrt x}\,dx$. (Exact value.)
drills.solution:
The integrand is unbounded at $x = 0$, so take a limit:
$$\lim_{t\to0^+}\int_t^{{b}}{k:coef}x^{-1/2}dx = \lim_{t\to0^+}\Big[{k2}\sqrt x\Big]_t^{{b}} = {k2}({rb}) - 0 = \mathbf{{I}}.$$
It converges because the exponent $\tfrac12 < 1$.

drills.title: Differentiate hyperbolic functions
drills.prompt: Differentiate $f(x) = {a}\cosh({k}x) {b:signed}\sinh({m}x^2)$.
drills.solution:
$(\cosh u)' = \sinh u\cdot u'$ and $(\sinh u)' = \cosh u\cdot u'$, with no minus signs.

- ${a}\cosh({k}x)$ has derivative ${a}\cdot\sinh({k}x)\cdot{k} = {ak}\sinh({k}x)$.
- ${b}\sinh({m}x^2)$ has derivative ${b}\cdot\cosh({m}x^2)\cdot{m}\cdot 2x$.

So $f'(x) =$ **${ak}\sinh({k}x) {bm2:signed}x\cosh({m}x^2)$**.

drills.title: Integral giving an inverse hyperbolic sine
drills.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^{{b}}\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2 + {a2}}}$. (Exact, like ln(3/2), or 4 decimals.)
drills.solution:
This is $\int\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2 + a^2}} = \sinh^{-1}\frac xa + C$ with $a = {a}$:
$$\int_0^{{b}}\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2 + {a2}}} = \sinh^{-1}\frac{{b}}{{a}} - \sinh^{-1}0 = \ln\left(\frac{{b}}{{a}} + \sqrt{\frac{{b}^2}{{a}^2} + 1}\right).$$
Since ${b}^2 + {a}^2 = {h}^2$, the root is $\frac{{h}}{{a}}$, so the value is $\ln\frac{{b} + {h}}{{a}} = \ln\left({r:texfrac}\right) \approx$ **{V:num4}**.

drills.title: Sag and length of a hanging cable
drills.prompt: A cable hangs in the shape $y = {a}\cosh\dfrac{x}{{a}}$ (meters) between supports at $x = -{b}$ and $x = {b}$. How far below the supports is its lowest point, and how long is the cable? (2 decimals)
drills.solution:
*Sag.* The supports are at height ${a}\cosh({ratio:num4}) \approx {top:num4}$ and the low point is at height ${a}\cosh 0 = {a}$. Sag $= {a}\left(\cosh({ratio:num4}) - 1\right) \approx$ **{sag:num2}** m.

*Length.* $y' = \sinh\frac{x}{{a}}$, so $\sqrt{1 + (y')^2} = \cosh\frac{x}{{a}}$ and
$$L = \int_{-{b}}^{{b}}\cosh\frac{x}{{a}}\,dx = {twoa}\sinh({ratio:num4}) \approx \mathbf{{L:num2}}\text{ m},$$
a little more than the {span}-meter gap.

drills.title: Euler's method, three steps
drills.prompt: Use Euler's method with step size $h = {h}$ to approximate $y({x3})$ for $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x {a:signedcoef}y$, $y(0) = {y0}$. (Three steps; 4 decimals.)

drills.title: Equilibria from a slope field
drills.prompt: The slope field below is for $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = (y {nr1:signed})({r2} - y)$. Find the stable and the unstable equilibrium solutions. Where does the solution with $y(0) = {y0}$ head as $x \to \infty$?
drills.solution:
Equilibria are where $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$: $y = {r1}$ and $y = {r2}$. Check signs: for ${r1} < y < {r2}$ both factors are positive, so solutions rise; above ${r2}$ the slope is negative, so solutions fall. Solutions on both sides move toward $y = {r2}$ (**stable**) and away from $y = {r1}$ (**unstable**; below it the slope is negative too, so solutions drop away). The solution starting at $y = {y0}$, between the two, rises toward **{r2}**.

(The field is drawn with slopes scaled by $\tfrac13$ to keep the segments readable; their directions are what matter.)

drills.title: Solve a separable equation
drills.prompt: Solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = {k:coef}{n}y$ with $y(0) = {A}$, then find $y({x1})$. (4 significant figures)
drills.solution: Separate: $\dfrac{dy}{y} = {k:coef}{n}\,dx$. Integrate: $\ln|y| = \dfrac{{k:coef}x^{{n1}}}{{n1}} + C$, so $y = Be^{{k:coef}x^{{n1}}/{n1}}$. At $x = 0$, $y = B = {A}$. So $y = {A:coef}e^{{k:coef}x^{{n1}}/{n1}}$ and $y({x1}) \approx$ **{y1:sig4}**.

drills.title: Exponential growth from two data points
drills.prompt: A population grows at a rate proportional to its size. It is {P0} at $t = 0$ and {P1:int} at $t = {t1}$ (years). When will it reach {goal:int}? (2 decimals)
drills.solution: $P = {P0}e^{kt}$. From $P({t1}) = {P1:dp0}$: $e^{{t1}k} = {ratio}$, so $k = \dfrac{\ln {ratio}}{{t1}} \approx {kr:num4}$. Solve ${P0}e^{kt} =$ {goal:int}: $e^{kt} = {target}$, $t = \dfrac{\ln {target}}{k} \approx$ **{T:num2}** years.

drills.title: Logistic model
drills.prompt: A population follows $\dfrac{dP}{dt} = {rate}P\left(1 - \dfrac{P}{{cap}}\right)$ with $P(0) = {P0:int}$. Find $P({t1})$ (nearest whole number) and the time when the population grows fastest (2 decimals).
drills.solution: $P(t) = \dfrac{M}{1 + Ae^{-kt}}$ with $M = {cap}$, $k = {rate}$, and $A = \dfrac{M - P_0}{P_0} = {A:num4}$. Then $P({t1}) = \dfrac{{cap}}{1 + {A:num4}e^{-{rate}\cdot{t1}}} \approx$ **{Pt:int}**. Growth is fastest when $P = \tfrac M2 = {half:int}$: $1 + Ae^{-kt} = 2$, so $t = \dfrac{\ln A}{{rate}} \approx$ **{th:num2}**.

drills.title: Solve a linear equation with an integrating factor
drills.prompt: Solve $xy' + {n}y = {c}{ex}$ for $x > 0$ with $y(1) = {y1}$, then find $y(2)$. (Exact fraction.)
drills.solution:
*Standard form:* divide by $x$ to get $y' + \dfrac{{n}}{x}y = \dfrac{{c}{ex}}{x}$, so $P(x) = \dfrac{{n}}{x}$.

*Integrating factor:* $\mu = e^{\int ({n}/x)\,dx} = e^{{n}\ln x} = x^{{n}}$.

Multiply through: $\left(x^{{n}}y\right)' = x^{{n}}\cdot\dfrac{{c}{ex}}{x} = {c}x^{{nm}}$, so $x^{{n}}y = \dfrac{{c}x^{{ne}}}{{ne}} + C$ and $y = \dfrac{{c}{ex}}{{ne}} + \dfrac{C}{x^{{n}}}$.

At $x = 1$: ${y1} = \dfrac{{c}}{{ne}} + C$, so $C = {Cc:texfrac}$. Then
$$y(2) = \frac{{c}\cdot{te}}{{ne}} + \frac{C}{{tn}} = \mathbf{{Y:texfrac}}.$$

drills.title: Salt in a mixing tank
drills.prompt: A tank holds {V:dp0} L of water containing {q0} kg of dissolved salt. Brine with {conc} kg of salt per liter flows in at {r} L/min, and the well-mixed solution drains at {r} L/min. How much salt is in the tank after {T} minutes (2 decimals), and how much in the long run?
drills.solution:
Rate in $= {conc}\times{r} = {rin}$ kg/min. Rate out $= \dfrac{Q}{{V:dp0}}\times{r} = \dfrac{Q}{{tau}}$ kg/min. So
$$\frac{dQ}{dt} + \frac{Q}{{tau}} = {rin}, \qquad Q(0) = {q0}.$$
This is $Q' + kQ = b$ with $k = \frac{1}{{tau}}$ and $b = {rin}$: the steady state is $\frac bk = {rin}\times{tau} = {Qss}$ kg, and
$$Q(t) = {Qss} {diff:signed}e^{-t/{tau}}.$$
At $t = {T}$: $Q = {Qss} {diff:signed}e^{-{expo}} \approx$ **{QT:num2}** kg. As $t \to \infty$ the transient dies out and $Q \to$ **{Qss}** kg ({conc} kg/L times {V:dp0} L).

drills.title: Current in an RL circuit
drills.prompt: A circuit with resistance $R = {R}\ \Omega$ and inductance $L = {Lh}$ H is connected to a {E}-volt battery at $t = 0$, so $I(0) = 0$. Find the current at $t = {t1}$ s, and the time when the current reaches 90% of its steady-state value. (3 decimals)
drills.solution:
$LI' + RI = E$ in standard form is $I' + {k:num4}I = {EL:num4}$. The steady state is $\frac ER = {Iss:num4}$ A and the time constant is $\frac LR = {tc:num4}$ s, so
$$I(t) = {Iss:num4}\left(1 - e^{-{k:num4}t}\right).$$
At $t = {t1}$: $I = {Iss:num4}\left(1 - e^{-{kt:num4}}\right) \approx$ **{It:dp3}** A.

90% of the steady state means $e^{-{k:num4}t} = 0.1$, so $t = \dfrac{\ln 10}{{k:num4}} \approx$ **{t90:dp3}** s.
